PullRequest.Title: issueReporter: simple and detailed layouts, and fewer steps to report
PullRequest.Body:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests

Makes the issue reporter quicker to fill in: a simple and a detailed layout, a shorter form, and a reporter window that opens next to the window it reports on. Together with the screenshot tool that is already in main, this replaces the draft #347591.

## Layouts

New experiment-controlled setting `issueReporter.wizard.layout`: `detailed`, the default, or `simple`. Both layouts ask for screenshots and the description first.

The simple layout:

- attaches a screenshot of the window being reported when a report opens;
- leaves out the target and category, except for extension reports;
- has one checkbox for all diagnostics;
- generates a missing title from the description, or takes the description's first line when no title arrives within 10 seconds.

The setting's experiment trigger is logged when a new report reads its layout. `issueReporter.previewClicked` now reports the layout, and whether the simple layout's automatic screenshot is still attached.

## A shorter form

- The attachment limits moved behind a "?" next to Attachments. Screenshots start from the floating bar or its shortcut, and the last card adds files.
- Images attached as files can be marked up like screenshots. Once they have annotations, they become screenshots that keep their file name.
- The description's guidance is its placeholder. The field starts as tall as the placeholder and grows with its text, and its Write and Preview tabs sit next to its label.

## Reporter window

- A reporter in its own window opens at the bottom right of the window it reports on.
- Closing it with a draft asks once, in the reporter's window, whether to discard the report. For this, the before-unload event of auxiliary windows gets `vetoSilently()`, for components that ask the user themselves.

## How to test

1. Run Help: Report Issue.... The reporter opens in its own window, at the bottom right of the window it reports on.
2. Paste an image into the attachments and click it to mark it up.
3. Type a description, then close the reporter window. It asks once whether to discard the report.
4. Set `issueReporter.wizard.layout` to `simple` and open a new report.

## Validation

- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `pnpm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- `node build/oxlint.ts` with the 17 TypeScript files that this PR changes: passed
- `node build/stylelint.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/issue/browser/media/issueReporterOverlay.css`: passed
- After `pnpm run build-fast --client-only`:
  - `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --runGlob "**/{screenshotTool,browserView,issue,imageCarousel,canvases}/test/**/*.test.js"`: 1031 passing, 3 pending
  - `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --runGlob "**/{workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser,sessions/contrib/chat/test}/**/*.test.js"`: 15976 passing, 24 pending, and 1 failing locally, `ChatListWidget` transcript streaming, which fails the same way without this PR and passes in CI
- Tried in Code OSS at d439eaa2ac9: the window placement, both layouts, the simple layout's automatic screenshot, the "?" help, capturing from the floating bar, and marking up a screenshot and a pasted image file, which keeps its file name. Closing a report with changes asked once whether to discard it, in the reporter's window while it had focus, and an untouched simple report closed without asking.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed await, 10-second bound, foreground model call chain, expected blank-title trigger, and before/after Preview behavior are all explicit in code and tests. Only the typical model duration and experiment prevalence are uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: One foreground language-model request, including extension registration/model selection and remote model response streaming
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each simple-layout report previewed with a blank title adds one uncached foreground model request; latency scales with cold extension/model activation and network/model response time, with the new timeout allowing 10 seconds before fallback.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Blocked Preview critical path and multi-second interaction latency before attachment upload/GitHub preview can begin.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Preview validation previously required a title and then synchronously built and submitted the draft; language-model title generation ran only when the user explicitly clicked the Generate button, so Preview itself did not initiate or await this remote work.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added await automatically invokes title generation when a simple report has no title. The listener waits for installed extensions, selects a Copilot model, and calls ChatUtilityModelService.sendRequest as a foreground request; generateTitleForPreview blocks submission until it resolves or the new 10-second timeout falls back.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line 1804 moves the pre-existing optional AI-title operation onto the mandatory Preview path for blank titles; the deleted submit implementation never requested or awaited title generation.
Findings.Title: Do not block Preview on title generation
Findings.Impact: The simple layout explicitly makes the title optional, so leaving it blank is the expected path. For users with a Copilot model, clicking Preview can now sit at “Generating title...” for network/model latency—up to 10 seconds—before the report can progress, even though a local first-line fallback is already available.
Findings.Evidence: issueReporterOverlay.ts:1804 awaits generateTitleForPreview before model update, body construction, and onDidSubmit. That method races requestGeneratedTitle against TITLE_GENERATION_TIMEOUT=10_000. issueReporterController routes the request through extensionService.whenInstalledExtensionsRegistered, selectLanguageModels, and chatUtilityModelService.sendRequest; ChatUtilityModelService marks this request non-background and calls languageModelsService.sendChatRequest. The added test explicitly advances 10,000 ms before observing submission.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep Preview non-blocking: start/debounce title generation while the user edits or leaves the description, consume it only if already ready, and otherwise immediately submit with getFallbackIssueTitle. Leave the existing Generate button for users who choose to wait explicitly.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The fixed delay, IPC/capture/encode/decode call chain, placement before all visible opening work, one-per-simple-report cardinality, and pre-diff absence are explicit in changed code. Exact capture duration varies by hardware and pixel count, affecting severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: A fixed 100 ms timer followed by one native IPC capturePage, full-window JPEG encoding/base64 conversion, and browser image decode
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Every new simple-layout report pays at least the fixed 100 ms delay; the capture, encoding, transferred bytes, base64 allocation, and decode grow with the source window's pixel count (notably on high-DPI/4K displays).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased time before the issue reporter editor or auxiliary window becomes visible, plus avoidable CPU and allocation pressure on that interaction.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this diff, the wizard created its input and opened the editor/auxiliary window directly; opening a report did not first wait for a screenshot or repaint timer.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: For every simple-layout report, openNewReporter now awaits captureWindow before it creates the input or starts opening either host. captureWindow({ afterRepaint: true }) waits 100 ms, crosses to Electron capturePage, JPEG-encodes the full window, converts it to a base64 data URL, and decodes that image before resolving.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added line 210 introduces `await this.screenshotToolService.captureWindow(sourceWindow, { afterRepaint: true })` ahead of all reporter construction/opening; no equivalent capture existed on this path before the PR.
Findings.Title: Open the reporter before doing the automatic capture
Findings.Impact: With the experimental simple layout selected, Help: Report Issue has a guaranteed extra 100 ms pause and then waits for a full-window native capture before showing any reporter UI. The delay and allocation cost are larger on high-resolution displays.
Findings.Evidence: nativeIssueFormService.ts:210 is before both createInstance and auxiliaryWindowService.open/editorService.openEditor. screenshotToolService.captureWindowArea first awaits REPAINT_DELAY=100, then awaits hostService.getScreenshot; NativeHostService forwards that across the native boundary to webContents.capturePage and toJPEG(95), after which the renderer base64-encodes and decode()s the full image. openingReporter also serializes concurrent opens, so none of this is off the user-visible critical path.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the automatic attachment, but remove it from the reporter's visible-open critical path: wait only for an actual next-paint/compositor signal instead of a fixed 100 ms and begin showing/constructing the reporter shell while capture processing completes, attaching the result asynchronously without allowing the reporter window into the source capture.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a fresh issue report in detailed or simple layout
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Detailed mode proceeds directly to input construction and editor/auxiliary-window opening. Simple mode now must finish the automatic source-window screenshot before either host begins opening, so the repaint delay, native capture, encoding, and decode are all on the visible-open critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Capture the full source window through nativeHostService/webContents.capturePage, JPEG-encode it, transfer bytes, base64-encode, and decode it in the renderer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-window capture for each fresh simple-layout report; zero in detailed layout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Fresh wizard reports opened without any screenshot boundary on this path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Introduces a fixed 100 ms repaint wait plus capture/encode/transfer/decode before reporter construction or opening can begin.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open an auxiliary native window when the configured location is a window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One auxiliary-window open per fresh window-hosted report; zero for editor-hosted reports.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same auxiliary-window open occurred directly, without first waiting for a screenshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Remains on the open critical path after the new screenshot completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One source window per fresh simple report; screenshot work and temporary bytes scale with captured device-pixel dimensions and display scale.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: NativeIssueFormService.openingReporter coalesces/serializes concurrent open requests. The simple path performs exactly one screenshot serially before one editor or auxiliary-window open.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no screenshot cache or coalescing beyond the open guard; every fresh simple report captures again. Detailed mode does not capture.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed ordering and the full IPC/encoding call chain are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The 100 ms floor is explicit; capture/encode/decode duration and allocation size vary by hardware, DPI, and window dimensions.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the simple path eagerly performs a delayed full-window capture before showing any reporter UI.

Scenarios.Scenario: Preview a simple report with an empty optional title, then upload/open it on GitHub
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Validation now awaits title generation before body construction, onDidSubmit, attachment upload, and opening GitHub. The title path waits for extension registration/model selection and a foreground model response, falling back only after 10 seconds. Existing attachment uploads and URL opening remain downstream.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send a Copilot utility language-model request and collect its streamed response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One foreground model request for each simple preview with a blank title; none when a title is present or the target is external.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Preview never initiated model work; generation occurred only after an explicit Generate-button click, and Preview required a title.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks all submission progress until response/failure or the explicit 10-second fallback timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read imported attachment files and hash their contents.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to five file reads/hashes on a cold preview; screenshots are decoded from retained data URLs instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same attachment reads/hashes occurred before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing serial work after title generation and before upload.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the GitHub repository and upload uncached attachments through the mobile upload API, then open the issue URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One repository resolution shared across the submission, then at most one sequential upload per uncached attachment (maximum five), followed by one URL open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cached, sequential attachment uploads and URL opening occurred after immediate validation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing submission work, now starts only after automatic title generation finishes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One title request per blank-title preview attempt; attachment processing remains capped at five attachments and scales with their byte sizes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The UI disables Preview while generating, so one title request is active for this reporter. It is a non-background utility request and is not placed behind the service's background limiter. Attachment reads/hashes/uploads remain serial, one file at a time.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Title requests pass no key and have no positive-result cache or pending-request coalescing key. Model registration/selection may be warm, but the response is still a fresh request. Attachment uploads retain their existing content/repository cache; warm retries skip successful uploads, while cold uploads remain sequential.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed await, foreground service behavior, no request key, downstream ordering, and the 10-second test are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users without an available model may fall back quickly; users with a warm fast model may see less than the 10-second cap. Network/model latency and experiment exposure affect prevalence, not the blocking mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: expected blank-title previews now synchronously wait on an uncached remote model operation despite having an immediate local fallback.

Scenarios.Scenario: Import, display, and mark up image attachments
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Importing still copies a file into reporter storage and builds a thumbnail. The changed click path decodes the retained thumbnail, opens one image editor, and only converts the file attachment to a screenshot after annotations; removing the file attachment schedules cleanup of its owned copy.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create reporter storage, write imported bytes, and later delete the owned copy when an annotated file becomes a screenshot or the input is disposed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One write and at most one cleanup delete per imported file, capped at five attachments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Image files were already copied and cleaned up; this PR adds a bounded user-triggered path that removes the copy after conversion to a screenshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Import writes are existing attachment-import work; cleanup after conversion is asynchronous and not a repeated hot-path operation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most five attachments. One decode/editor operation per clicked image; decode cost scales with that thumbnail's dimensions and bytes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: attachmentsBeingEdited prevents duplicate editor starts for the same attachment. Different attachments can be edited independently, but this requires separate user actions rather than an automatic burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The thumbnail data URL is retained with the attachment and reused; there is no separate decoded-image cache. Imported-copy cleanup is owned by DisposableMap and occurs on removal or input disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for bounded cardinality, duplicate suppression, and cleanup ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Individual image dimensions vary, but attachment count is tightly capped and actions are user-triggered.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the new edit work is explicit user-requested work, bounded by attachment count, and cleanup does not accumulate.

Scenarios.Scenario: Type and resize the report form
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Description input uses native field-sizing: content, so browser sizing/layout occurs as text changes, capped visually at 400 px. Auxiliary-window resize continues to call controller.layout once per resize event.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Text length and input frequency control native textarea measurement; visible growth stops at the 400 px maximum height.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous browser UI work occurs on the input/resize event sequence; no async fan-out or expensive process/network boundary is reached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache applies; browser layout state is reused internally.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Moderate for per-input layout work, insufficient for a concrete regression finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The browser's field-sizing implementation cost for very large pasted descriptions is not quantified, and the diff provides no evidence of a realistic jank threshold.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: bounded native control sizing alone does not establish actionable rendering jank.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close an auxiliary reporter with unsaved changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The before-unload listener silently vetoes the first close, then the coalesced close operation waits for readiness, focuses the reporter window if needed, and opens the existing discard confirmation. Focus waits for an event with a 500 ms cap.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Focus the auxiliary native window before showing the discard dialog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one focus request per coalesced unsaved-close attempt, only when the reporter document lacks focus.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The discard confirmation was shown without explicitly focusing and waiting for the reporter window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Can add focus latency, capped at 500 ms, before the dialog; this is intentional placement work rather than repeated scaling work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One focus attempt and one dialog per coalesced close operation, independent of report size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: confirmOperation coalesces overlapping close confirmations for a reporter; no burst occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache; operation coalescing prevents duplicate concurrent confirmation work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the bounded wait and coalescing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Focus normally emits promptly; the full 500 ms occurs only when no focus event arrives.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the new focus boundary is bounded, only runs on an explicit unsaved-close action, and preserves required dialog ownership without multiplicative work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 18 changed files and all diff pages. Reported two eager critical-path regressions: delayed full-window capture before simple reporter opening, and foreground language-model title generation before Preview. Checked attachment upload cardinality/cache behavior, image-edit cleanup, native close focus coalescing, and form layout work; no other changed mechanism met the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
